questions.knowledge_point: Computing Iterations of the Newton-Raphson Method Using Linear Systems
questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,2]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-4{y}^{3}-1 \\ {x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-2\end{aligned}].
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting  at the point $[1,\,1]^{T}.$

| $[$ | $3$ | {{field-1}} | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | $4$ | $].$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} | $8$ | {{field-3}} |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-4{y}^{3}-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-4{y}^{3}-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & -12{y}^{2} \\ 2x & 8y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & -12{y}^{2} \\ 2x & 8y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-4{y}^{3}-1 \\ {x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & -12{y}^{2} \\ 2x & 8y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-4{y}^{3}-1 \\ {x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2} & -12(1)^{2} \\ 2(1) & 8(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}-4(1)^{3}-1 \\ (1)^{2}+4(1)^{2}-2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & -12 \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,0]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-7 \\ {x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-8\end{aligned}].
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting  at the point $[-1,\,1]^{T}.$

| $[$ | $-6$ | $2$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | {{field-1}} | $].$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} | $3$ |  |  |  |

The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-7) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-7) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-8) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-8)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6x & 2y \\ 2x & 8y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6x & 2y \\ 2x & 8y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-7 \\ {x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-8\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6x & 2y \\ 2x & 8y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-7 \\ {x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}-8\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6(-1) & 2(1) \\ 2(-1) & 8(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}3(-1)^{2}+(1)^{2}-7 \\ (-1)^{2}+4(1)^{2}-8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,2]\times [1,3]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y-4y+6 \\ xy-2\end{aligned}].
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point  $[0,\,1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration.

| $[$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | {{field-3}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $0$ | $2$ |  |  |  |

| ${x}_{1}=[$ | $2$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-4}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as 

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y-4y+6) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y-4y+6) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2xy & {x}^{2}-4 \\ y & x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}2xy & {x}^{2}-4 \\ y & x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y-4y+6 \\ xy-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}2xy & {x}^{2}-4 \\ y & x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y-4y+6 \\ xy-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}2(0)(1) & {0}^{2}-4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}(0)^{2}(1)-4(1)+6 \\ (0)(1)-2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0.5\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0.5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0.5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,2]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4 \\ {x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[0,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-1.5,\,1.5]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{2}\,≈[$ | $-1.198$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-1}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 3{y}^{2}-x \\ 4{x}^{3}-2y & -2x+2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 3{y}^{2}-x \\ 4{x}^{3}-2y & -2x+2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4 \\ {x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 3{y}^{2}-x \\ 4{x}^{3}-2y & -2x+2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4 \\ {x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(-1.5)-1.5 & 3(1.5)^{2}-(-1.5) \\ 4(-1.5)^{3}-2(1.5) & -2(-1.5)+2(1.5)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-1.5)^{2}+{1.5}^{3}-(-1.5)\cdot 1.5-4 \\ (-1.5)^{4}-2(-1.5)(1.5)+{1.5}^{2}-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-4.5 & 8.25 \\ -16.5 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3.875 \\ 6.8125\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{-4.5\cdot 6-8.25\cdot (-16.5)}[\begin{aligned}6 & -8.25 \\ 16.5 & -4.5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3.875 \\ 6.8125\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{109.125}[\begin{aligned}-32.953\,125 \\ 33.281\,250\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-1.198 \\ 1.195\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-3,-1]\times [-4,-1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+xy+{y}^{2}-12 \\ {x}^{3}+x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,-1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-1.4,\,-3.6]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{2}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+xy+{y}^{2}-12) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xy+{y}^{2}-12) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+x-y) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+x-y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x+y & x+2y \\ 3{x}^{2}+1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x+y & x+2y \\ 3{x}^{2}+1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+xy+{y}^{2}-12 \\ {x}^{3}+x-y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2x+y & x+2y \\ 3{x}^{2}+1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+xy+{y}^{2}-12 \\ {x}^{3}+x-y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ -3.6\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(-1.4)+(-3.6) & (-1.4)+2(-3.6) \\ 3(-1.4)^{2}+1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-1.4)^{2}+(-1.4)(-3.6)+(-3.6)^{2}-12 \\ (-1.4)^{3}+(-1.4)-(-3.6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ -3.6\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-6.4 & -8.6 \\ 6.88 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}7.96 \\ -0.544\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ -3.6\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-6.4)\cdot (-1)-(-8.6)\cdot (6.88)}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 8.6 \\ -6.88 & -6.4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7.96 \\ -0.544\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ -3.6\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{65.568}[\begin{aligned}-12.6384 \\ -51.2832\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-1.207 \\ -2.818\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
